name: Keeper
tagline: Zero-knowledge password manager for individuals, families and businesses, with optional dark-web monitoring and privileged access add-ons.
bestFor: Businesses that want password management with compliance certifications and PAM add-ons
description: Keeper stores passwords, passkeys, identities and payment cards in an encrypted vault that syncs across desktop, mobile, browser extensions and a web app. Keeper Unlimited costs $42.99 per year ($3.58 per month) for one user, and business plans start at $2 per user per month billed annually.
pros: Native desktop apps for Windows, macOS and Linux as well as iOS, Android, browser extensions and a web vault
Family plan covers 5 users with private vaults and includes 10 GB of encrypted file storage for $91.99 per year
Business plan includes a free Family plan for every user
Holds SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001/27017/27018 certifications, and its government cloud is FedRAMP High
cons: BreachWatch dark-web monitoring is a paid add-on ($26.99 per year) on Personal and Family plans
Free tier is limited to one mobile device and 10 records, according to Security.org
Business Starter is capped at 5–10 users; SSO/SAML, SCIM and role-based access control need the Enterprise plan
freePlanDetails: Keeper Free: mobile app only, one mobile device, 10 records for passwords or passkeys, no cloud backup, emergency access or support (as reported by Security.org, updated 2026-04-17). Not listed on Keeper's pricing page.
trial: 30-day free trial for personal and family plans; free trials for Business, Enterprise and KeeperPAM (length not stated on the business pricing page)

plans.name: Free
plans.notes: Mobile only, one device, 10 records (reported by Security.org, 2026-04-17).

plans.name: Personal (Keeper Unlimited)
plans.notes: $42.99 billed annually; 1 user, unlimited devices and password storage, 24/7 support. BreachWatch add-on $26.99/year; Secure File Storage add-on from $13.99/year.

plans.name: Family
plans.notes: $91.99 billed annually for 5 users with private vaults; includes 10 GB Secure File Storage and emergency access. BreachWatch add-on $26.99/year.

plans.name: Business Starter
plans.notes: Per user per month billed annually; for 5–10 users. Encrypted vault, admin console, sharing and autofill.

plans.name: Business
plans.notes: Per user per month billed annually; adds shared team folders, delegated administration and a free Family plan for every user.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Listed at $6.00 per user per month billed annually with a Request a Quote button; adds SCIM, AD/LDAP, SSO/SAML provisioning, advanced 2FA, RBAC and developer APIs. KeeperPAM is sales-only with custom pricing.

integrations: SCIM, Active Directory/LDAP and SSO/SAML provisioning (Enterprise); developer APIs; Secrets Manager CLI and SDKs, CI/CD and IaC integrations, ITSM and SIEM integrations as add-ons

name: RoboForm
tagline: Long-running password manager and form filler from Siber Systems, with a free single-device plan and low-cost Premium, Family and Business tiers.
bestFor: Individuals who want a cheap password manager with strong form filling
description: RoboForm saves and autofills passwords, passkeys and web forms, with a free plan for unlimited passwords on one device. Premium renews at $29.88 per year ($2.49 per month), and Business costs $39.95 per user per year ($3.33 per month).
pros: Free plan stores unlimited passwords on a single device, with 2FA, compromised-password alerts and a built-in TOTP authenticator
Premium includes data-breach monitoring for 5 email addresses, emergency access and an optional local-only mode
Business includes SSO, SCIM provisioning and role-based access control, plus a Family plan for staff when 10+ licences are bought
Enterprise offers a self-hosting model for environments of 1,000+ users
cons: No native Linux app; downloads cover Windows, Mac, iOS, Android and browsers
Free plan has no sync across devices, no web access and no sharing
Advertised sale prices apply to the first year only; Premium renews at $29.88 and Family at $47.75 per year
freePlanDetails: Unlimited passwords on a single device; advanced 2FA, compromised-password monitoring, integrated TOTP authenticator, passwordless unlock and cloud backup. No multi-device access, web access, breach monitoring, emergency access or sharing.
trial: Business: 14-day free trial for up to 30 users, extendable once by 5 days, no credit card. Personal plans: 30-day money-back guarantee.

plans.name: Free
plans.notes: Single device, unlimited passwords; 24/7 email support.

plans.name: Premium
plans.notes: Regular price $29.88/year. Black Friday promo (ends Nov 30, 2026): new users pay $18.00 for the first year ($1.50/month), then renews at $29.88. Unlimited devices, breach monitoring for 5 emails, priority email support plus weekday live chat and phone.

plans.name: Family
plans.notes: Up to 5 Premium accounts. Regular price $47.75/year; promo $28.65 for the first year for new users, then renews at $47.75.

plans.name: Business
plans.notes: Per user; regular $39.95/user/year. Promo $23.97 for the first year for new users, then renews at $39.95. Multi-year discount available. Includes SSO, SCIM, RBAC and a Family plan for personal use with 10+ paid licences.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Custom volume-based pricing; dedicated onboarding, custom SLA, self-hosting model for 1,000+ users.

integrations: Single sign-on (SSO) and SCIM provisioning (Business); MSP portal

name: Enpass
tagline: Password manager that keeps your encrypted vault in your own cloud storage or on your device instead of on Enpass servers.
bestFor: People who want to keep their vault in their own cloud storage
description: Enpass stores passwords, passkeys and cards in an encrypted vault that syncs through your own iCloud, Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Box or Nextcloud, never on Enpass servers. A free plan covers 25 items, Premium renews at $23.99 per year ($1.99 per month), and a one-time Lifetime licence costs $99.99.
pros: Vault is stored in your own cloud account or locally, never on Enpass servers
One-time Lifetime licence for $99.99 as an alternative to a subscription
Native apps for Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS and Android, plus Apple Watch and Wear OS
Business plan is $1.99 per user per month and includes SSO, SCIM and SIEM integration
cons: Free plan is limited to 25 items in one vault
No web app; access is through native apps and browser extensions
Breach and dark-web monitoring is not included in the Free plan
freePlanDetails: Up to 25 items in 1 vault, 1 account, import limited to 25 items.
trial: Business: 30-day free trial, no credit card required

name: LastPass
tagline: Cloud password manager with personal, family and business plans, a free tier and built-in dark web monitoring.
bestFor: Small businesses that want simple admin controls at a low per-user price
description: LastPass stores passwords, passkeys and notes in a cloud vault that is reached through browser extensions, desktop and mobile apps and a web vault. A free plan works on one device type, Premium costs $3 per month billed annually, and business plans start at $4.25 per user per month.
pros: Free plan includes unlimited password storage, autofill and dark web monitoring
Families covers 6 Premium accounts for $4 per month billed annually
Business plan includes a free Families account for every employee
Lists ISO 27001, ISO 27701, SOC 2 Type II and BSI C5 certifications
cons: In the 2022 breach, attackers copied backups of customer vault data, including encrypted passwords and unencrypted website URLs (LastPass notice and TechCrunch, December 2022)
Free plan works on either desktop or mobile, not both, and shares one password with one person at a time
No native Linux app; the VPN in the Plus plan runs on Windows only
freePlanDetails: Limited to 1 device type (desktop or mobile). Unlimited password storage, autofill, dark web monitoring, basic sharing (one password with one person at a time); self-service support only; includes a 30-day Premium trial.
trial: 30 days for personal plans, 14 days for business plans; no credit card required

name: KeePassXC
tagline: Free, open-source, offline password manager for Windows, macOS and Linux that stores your vault in a local KeePass database file.
bestFor: Privacy-minded desktop users who want a free offline vault
description: KeePassXC is a community-built, GPLv3-licensed port of KeePass that keeps passwords in a local encrypted database file, with browser integration and passkey support through the KeePassXC-Browser extension. It is free; there are no paid plans.
pros: Free and open source under GPLv3, with no account or subscription
Vault is a local database file you control; sync it with any cloud folder if you want
Supports passkeys through the KeePassXC-Browser extension (since version 2.7.7)
Database reports include password health and an on-demand Have I Been Pwned check
cons: No official mobile apps; the project points to third-party KeePass apps such as KeePassDX, KeePass2Android, Strongbox and KeePassium
No built-in sync, sharing or web vault
No continuous breach monitoring or email alias features
freePlanDetails: Fully free open-source software (GPLv3); donations accepted.

plans.name: Free (open source)
plans.notes: All features free; latest stable release 2.8.0 (21 October 2026).

integrations: KeePassXC-Browser extension; keepassxc-cli; database files usable in third-party KeePass apps (KeePassDX, KeePass2Android, Strongbox, KeePassium)
